issues.legal_issue: A prosecution for nonconforming building use cannot be quashed merely because a court, on reading the planning document alone, concludes that it does not specify the building’s use where that determination depends on the full evidence.
material_facts: The respondents were being prosecuted for allegedly using land or buildings contrary to a planning document under a statutory planning scheme.
The High Court quashed the prosecutions after concluding that the planning document did not specify the use of the buildings.

The High Court did not determine the issue on the evidence as a whole; the question whether the document specified the use of each building depended on facts and circumstances to be assessed in the pending prosecutions.
issues.conclusion: The High Court should not have quashed the prosecutions on that basis. The prosecutions must proceed to conclusion according to law, without any determination by the Supreme Court on whether the planning document specified the use of the buildings.
issues.legal_principle: Whether a planning document specifies a particular use for a particular building, and whether the accused incurred penal liability, is primarily for the criminal court to determine on the entire evidence. A High Court may protect a person from an illegal or vexatious prosecution by writ or through its inherent or revisional powers in an appropriate case, but these were not such cases. The prosecution bears the burden of proving the charge under Sections 14 and 29(2) of the Delhi Development Act, 1957; the accused must have an opportunity to contest whether the necessary ingredients have been proved.

predicates.criminal_prosecution_pending: A person was facing a pending criminal prosecution for an alleged planning-use violation.
predicates.high_court_quashed_before_trial: A High Court terminated the prosecution before the criminal court assessed the case on the evidence.
predicates.planning_document_issue_depends_on_full_: Whether the planning document specified the relevant use depended on facts and circumstances beyond reading that document alone.
predicates.prosecution_must_proceed_to_adjudication: The prosecution must continue to a decision by the criminal court according to law.

issues.definition: When a pending prosecution is quashed before trial on a planning-document issue that depends on the full evidence, the prosecution must proceed to adjudication.

issues.legal_issue: The prohibition on using land or a building contrary to a planning document applies after any relevant plan comes into operation and extends to building use where the plan specifies that use.
material_facts: A master plan had come into operation in the relevant areas, while the zonal development plans had not yet come into operation.
The alleged violations concerned uses of buildings said to be inconsistent with the master plan.
The Supreme Court did not decide whether the master plan in fact specified the use of any particular building.
issues.conclusion: The statutory prohibition applies after any plan comes into operation and covers use of a building as well as use of land; whether the master plan specified the use of a particular building remained for the criminal court to decide.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14 of the Delhi Development Act, 1957 prohibits use of land or a building otherwise than in conformity with any plan that has come into operation. The prohibition is subject to the statutory proviso permitting continuation, on prescribed terms and conditions, of an existing use. The Court expressed no view on whether the master plan specified the use of the particular buildings in these cases.

rule.if: planning_use_enforcement_case and plan_in_force and building_use_conflicts_with_plan and not protected_existing_use

predicates.planning_use_enforcement_case: A proceeding concerns alleged use of land or a building contrary to a planning document.
predicates.plan_in_force: A relevant planning document has come into operation for the area.
predicates.building_use_conflicts_with_plan: The use of a building is contrary to a use specified for it by the planning document.
predicates.protected_existing_use: The building is being used in a manner covered by the protection for continuation of an existing use.
predicates.nonconforming_building_use_is_prohibited: The building may not be used in a manner that conflicts with the planning document.

issues.definition: When a relevant plan is in force and a building’s use conflicts with it, the use is prohibited unless it is protected as a continuing existing use.

issues.legal_issue: In a criminal prosecution for a statutory planning-use violation, the prosecution bears the burden of proving the elements necessary to establish guilt.
material_facts: The respondents faced prosecutions for alleged violations of the statutory restriction on land or building use.
The Supreme Court stated that the prosecution had the burden of proving all matters required to establish guilt.
The accused were entitled to defend themselves and show that necessary elements had not been proved.
issues.conclusion: The prosecution must prove all elements necessary to establish guilt; the accused must be given an opportunity to contest that proof.
issues.legal_principle: For an offence under Section 29(2) based on an alleged violation of Section 14 of the Delhi Development Act, 1957, the onus is on the prosecution to prove the matters required to establish the offence. The accused may defend themselves by showing that necessary ingredients have not been proved or established.

predicates.criminal_prosecution_for_planning_use_vi: A person is prosecuted for an alleged violation of a restriction on planning-related land or building use.
predicates.prosecution_must_prove_offense_elements: The prosecution must prove the facts necessary to establish the charged offence.

issues.definition: In a criminal prosecution for a planning-use violation, the prosecution must prove the facts necessary to establish the offence.
